questions.title: Does the MLP ranker beat the linear ranker on the same deck shell?
questions.why: Non-linear supervised action ranking may capture interactions the linear scorer misses, but smoke payoff must separate model effect from deck and mulligan effect.
questions.next_test: Same-deck pilot variants: linear_ranker_rev0021 vs mlp_ranker_rev0023 vs blended MLP across at least three shells.

questions.title: Which mulligan policy moves results most by shell?
questions.why: The rev0023 gate shows mulligan choice can swing same-shell scores. Learned agents should not hide this parameter.
questions.next_test: Train a public mulligan ranker over explicit keep/take/bottom choices and evaluate as deck + mulligan + pilot.

questions.title: Can a ranker improve by learning from winners rather than imitating policies?
questions.why: Imitation reproduces weak/readable agents. A stronger ranker may need outcome-weighted examples or policy-improvement data.
questions.next_test: Collect promoted traces, weight chosen actions by final outcome and opponent strength, retrain, and compare under the promotion gate.

questions.title: Where should C++ acceleration move next?
questions.why: C++ trace checks are now stable on sampled traffic, but full rollout could split semantic authority if rushed.
questions.next_test: Batch rollout sketch that keeps Python-generated trace/replay labels and measures Python shell overhead separately from C++ transition cost.

questions.title: Does 40-life construction reward different mulligan aggression?
questions.why: Life total and mulligan decisions interact: Force life cost, Overlord clock speed, and Jace decking pressure all change with starting life.
questions.next_test: Run mulligan policy gate split by life total and shell, then compare shell-specific policy rankings.
